title: Domino: Decoupling Causal Modeling from Autoregressive Drafting
hook: Speculative decoding is stuck between fast-but-sloppy parallel drafters and accurate-but-slow autoregressive ones. Domino splits the difference and hits up to 5.8× throughput.
key_points: A parallel backbone drafts a whole block of tokens at once — cheap, but weak at intra-block dependencies.
A lightweight 'Domino head' then refines that draft with prefix-dependent causal information.
A base-anchored curriculum first trains the parallel backbone, then shifts toward the causally corrected output.
On Qwen3 models: up to 5.49× end-to-end speedup, and 5.8× throughput under SGLang serving.
content_html: Speculative decoding speeds up LLM generation by drafting several tokens cheaply and verifying them in one pass of the big model. But there's a tension in how you draft: an autoregressive drafter models the dependencies between draft tokens well, yet pays a sequential cost per token; a parallel drafter is fast but produces a weaker draft because it ignores those dependencies. Domino proposes a way to get both.
extra_html:
How it works

Domino decouples causal modeling from the expensive autoregressive execution. A parallel "backbone" first emits preliminary distributions for an entire block of draft tokens in one shot. A small, lightweight "Domino head" then refines those distributions using prefix-dependent causal information — recovering the intra-block dependencies the parallel draft missed, without re-running a full autoregressive pass. To keep training stable, the authors use a base-anchored curriculum: first strengthen the parallel backbone, then gradually shift optimization toward the causally corrected final distribution.

Why it matters

Drafting quality versus drafting cost is the central trade-off that bounds how much speculative decoding can actually accelerate serving. By moving the causal correction into a cheap refinement head, Domino reports up to 5.49× end-to-end speedup on Qwen3 under the Transformers backend and up to 5.8× throughput under SGLang — meaningful gains for production inference where latency and cost dominate.
